body:
## Summary

A version-pinned upgrade installed an authenticated root instruction block that violated an existing one-physical-line Markdown rule and left the installer-adjusted whole-file word ceiling below the resulting file size.

## Expected

An authenticated upgrade should preserve configured project verification: managed prose should satisfy common Markdown policies or provide an exact ownership-aware integration mechanism, and any installer-authored budget adjustment should cover the actual merged file without granting uncontrolled headroom.

## Observed

The managed block contained hard-wrapped prose while its byte hash prohibited local reformatting. The upgrade changed the root ceiling to 2800, but the merged file contained 2858 words: 909 managed and 1949 project-owned. Default documentation verification failed until the project added authenticated region masking and froze the whole-file ceiling at 2858.

## Impact

Post-upgrade readiness was blocked and required a reviewed project-local checker contract, negative tests, documentation updates, and another complete verification cycle even though the installed activation set was healthy.

## Hypothesis

The managed payload formatting and budget adjustment were validated against Kit installation integrity but not against the final merged instruction file and repository-owned documentation gates.

## Proposed iteration

Keep managed prose on one physical line per paragraph where practical, publish a stable ownership-aware region contract for project gates, and compute or validate any project budget adaptation against the actual merged file before reporting upgrade health.

## Generic reproduction

1. In an existing repository, enforce one physical line per Markdown paragraph and a whole-file word ceiling for root AGENTS.md. Upgrade and activate the version-pinned Kit, then run the configured documentation checks. Observe managed-block wrap violations and a merged word count above the installer-adjusted ceiling while doctor still reports the authenticated installation healthy.

## Sanitized evidence

- The exact managed region was 909 words, project-owned prose remained 1949 words, the merged file was 2858 words, and the adjusted ceiling was 2800. Three hard-wrapped paragraphs were inside the authenticated managed region. Doctor reported matching hashes, so modifying those bytes was not a valid repair.

## Classification

- Kind: `compatibility`
- Component: `upgrade managed AGENTS adapter`
- Severity: `medium`
- Confidence: `high`
- Trigger: `Independent default verification and documentation synchronization failed immediately after an otherwise healthy authenticated upgrade.`
- Occurrences in this project: `1`

## Minimal environment

- Vibe Kit: `0.8.0`
- Workflow: `post-upgrade activation and default verification`
- Agent role: `workflow orchestrator`
- Runtime: `Python 3.14`
- Platform family: `Darwin`

## Privacy

- Status: `clean`
- Public submission: `allowed`
- Raw code, logs, prompts, conversations and environment values are not included.

title: [Vibe Kit feedback] Managed AGENTS block can invalidate project documentation gates after upgrade

body:
## Summary

The readiness workflow allowed project notes marked implemented to satisfy covered-by-accepted-decision even though only Accepted ADRs are eligible.

## Expected

The gate should distinguish lifecycle-complete project notes from Accepted ADRs and refuse implementation-ready when the governing decision is not an Accepted ADR.

## Observed

A readiness specialist treated two implemented notes as accepted decisions and released implementation; independent QA detected the invalid coverage basis after edits had begun.

## Impact

The correct edits had to be fully reverted and repeated after a new pre-implementation gate, delaying readiness and creating avoidable verification work.

## Hypothesis

The written rule is clear, but persisted readiness records and role guidance lack a machine-checkable guard or explicit negative example for implemented project notes.

## Proposed iteration

Validate covered-by-accepted-decision references as Accepted ADRs before an implementation-ready release, and add a negative example plus QA check for implemented notes.

## Generic reproduction

1. Start a medium maintenance task, cite a project note whose lifecycle status is implemented, record covered-by-accepted-decision, and observe whether the workflow releases implementation without an Accepted ADR.

## Sanitized evidence

- Independent QA found the invalid coverage basis after implementation began; all implementation surfaces were reverted, the baseline was confirmed, and a valid no-new-durable-decision gate was issued before reimplementation.

## Classification

- Kind: `workflow-gap`
- Component: `technical-decision-readiness`
- Severity: `medium`
- Confidence: `high`
- Trigger: `Independent QA detected that implemented project notes had been treated as Accepted ADRs after implementation was released.`
- Occurrences in this project: `1`

## Minimal environment

- Vibe Kit: `0.7.0`
- Workflow: `vibe-debug-flow`
- Agent role: `vibe-tech-lead`
- Runtime: `Python 3.14`
- Platform family: `Darwin`
